title: The AI Industry Should Make Something People Want
gist: Paywalled teaser: Brian Judge argues AI companies, epitomized by OpenAI's Sam Altman, have alienated Americans by imposing the costs of their products and treating consent as optional; with voters rejecting data centers, the incoming Congress has an opening for meaningful AI regulation.

themes.theme: Public backlash against AI and data centers

insights.claim: AI companies have alienated Americans by forcing them to bear the costs of their products while treating their consent as optional.
insights.speaker: Brian Judge
insights.so_what: Social license for AI is eroding, a growing political risk for AI infrastructure build-out.
insights.quote: forcing them to bear the costs of their products while treating their consent as optional

insights.claim: Voters across the United States are rejecting data centers, creating an opportunity for the incoming Congress to enact meaningful AI regulation and hold the industry accountable.
insights.speaker: Brian Judge
insights.so_what: Local opposition and possible federal regulation could slow data-center permitting and raise costs for hyperscalers and AI developers.
insights.quote: With voters across the United States rejecting data centers

insights.claim: Sam Altman, whose Y Combinator urged founders to 'make something people want,' has not followed that advice as CEO of OpenAI.
insights.speaker: Brian Judge
insights.so_what: Questions product-market fit and public demand underlying OpenAI-led AI investment narratives.
insights.quote: As CEO of OpenAI, however, Altman has not followed his own advice.
insights.locator: BERKELEY—When Sam Altman ran Y Combinator
